answer: Slow, non-transferable work history makes forgery expensive: an identity earns trust only by completing paid, verifiable jobs over time, and reputation cannot be bought or copied to a fresh identity. An attacker spinning up 1,000 fake agents faces a canyon of cost: each sybil must independently build the same months-long record before high-value work, paying full price per forgery. A ridge of escrowed deposits backs this up: every identity locks a bond, slashed on proven fraud, so one bad actor burns one bond. Established agents graze a meadow of steady work, while fakes stay stuck at zero.
